description: Patients who have had a negative urine protein result on some lab test and a negative rheumatoid factor result on some lab test, not necessarily the same one.

b.request: For patients present in the Patient table who have at least one lab record with `U-PRO = '-'` and at least one lab record with `RA = '-'` (the results may be from different lab records), return each patient's ID, sex, average `ALP`, and average `HCT` across all their lab records, ignoring missing values and without rounding; group by patient ID and sex, sort by average `HCT` descending with missing averages last, and return the top 10.
b.sql:
SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALP) AS average_ALP, AVG(l.HCT) AS average_HCT
FROM Patient AS p
JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS u WHERE u.ID = p.ID AND u.`U-PRO` = '-')
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS r WHERE r.ID = p.ID AND r.RA = '-')
GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
ORDER BY average_HCT IS NULL ASC, average_HCT DESC
LIMIT 10;
b.raw: For patients present in the Patient table who have at least one lab record with `U-PRO = '-'` and at least one lab record with `RA = '-'` (the results may be from different lab records), return each patient's ID, sex, average `ALP`, and average `HCT` across all their lab records, ignoring missing values and without rounding; group by patient ID and sex, sort by average `HCT` descending with missing averages last, and return the top 10.

d.request: List the top 10 patients present in the Patient table who have at least one lab record with `U-PRO = '-'` and at least one lab record with `RA = '-'`, which may be different records; report each patient’s ID, sex, and the unrounded averages of `ALP` and `HCT` across all their lab records, ignoring missing values, grouped by ID and sex and sorted by average `HCT` descending with missing averages last.
d.sql:
SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALP) AS avg_ALP, AVG(l.HCT) AS avg_HCT
FROM Patient AS p
JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS u
    WHERE u.ID = p.ID AND u.`U-PRO` = '-'
)
AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS r
    WHERE r.ID = p.ID AND r.RA = '-'
)
GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
ORDER BY avg_HCT IS NULL, avg_HCT DESC
LIMIT 10

a.request: For patients who have a laboratory record with `U-PRO` of '-' and a laboratory record (possibly a different one) with `RA` of '-', list each patient's ID, their sex (from the Patient table, only patients present there), and the average `ALP` and average `HCT` across all of their lab records (ignoring missing values, unrounded). Group by patient ID and sex, sort by average `HCT` from highest to lowest with missing averages last, and show the top 10.
a.sql:
SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALP) AS avg_ALP, AVG(l.HCT) AS avg_HCT
FROM Patient AS p
LEFT JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
WHERE p.ID IN (
    SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` = '-'
)
AND p.ID IN (
    SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE RA = '-'
)
GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
ORDER BY avg_HCT IS NULL ASC, avg_HCT DESC
LIMIT 10;

c.request: For patients who have tested '-' for both urine protein (`U-PRO`) and rheumatoid factor (`RA`), list each patient's ID, their sex (from the Patient table, only patients present there), and the average `ALP` and average `HCT` across all of their lab records (ignoring missing values, unrounded). Group by patient ID and sex, sort by average `HCT` from highest to lowest with missing averages last, and show the top 10. Patients who have had a negative urine protein result on some lab test and a negative rheumatoid factor result on some lab test, not necessarily the same one.
c.sql:
WITH eligible_patients AS (
    SELECT ID
    FROM Laboratory
    GROUP BY ID
    HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN `U-PRO` = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
       AND SUM(CASE WHEN RA = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
)
SELECT p.ID, p.SEX,
       AVG(l.ALP) AS avg_ALP,
       AVG(l.HCT) AS avg_HCT
FROM eligible_patients e
JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID
JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID
GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
ORDER BY avg_HCT DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;
